summary: Financial document recognition is often assessed using character and word error rates, although these metrics do not express whether a system preserves the financial facts on which people and organisations act. This paper develops a human-centred, risk-constrained framework for evaluating financial document recognition as evidence recovery and decision support.
takeaways: This paper develops a human-centred, risk-constrained framework for evaluating financial document recognition as evidence recovery and decision support.
A layered quality model covers text, localization, layout, tables, fields, fact correctness, evidence grounding, uncertainty, robustness, and operational performance.
The contribution is theoretical and methodological; no new model, dataset, or empirical performance result is claimed.
